transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-23
Time: 17:00 UTC (PDT 09:00, CET 18:00)
Duration: ~55 minutes
Location: All-hands company-wide (Zoom)
Attendees: Aria, Noah, Maya, Ethan, Sofia, Julian, Priya, Liam + company

Auto-summary: Quick financial update, product roadmap highlights (Dedicated GA timeline, Private pilot expansion), infra perf wins, hiring update, and AMA. Several links shared in chat (roadmap deck, Q1 metrics spreadsheet, benchmarking doc).

[00:00] Aria Nakamura: Hey everyone, good morning, good afternoon, good evening. Thanks for joining the Feb all-hands, we'll keep to an hour. Quick one, we got a big month behind us — Q1 track is looking solid. Uh, Maya will lead product, then Noah on infra, then Sofia on research, then quick ops notes, and we'll open for Q&A.

[00:38] Maya Patel: Thanks Aria. I'll kick off with the product highlights. So, roadmap — we're on track to GA Dedicated for early April. That means reserved capacity, nicer autoscale policies, and the SLA stuff, um, the SLA wording is in the draft deck in the chat. We shipped the first round of perf profiles for the quantized variants last week. There's still a bit of noise in the perf profiles for some of the 8-bit runs, likely kernel selection w/ newer CUDA drivers, so Noah's team is on it.

[01:20] Speaker 1: Quick clarifying q — when you say GA for Dedicated, is that GA for the billing surface or GA for the whole stack incl private?

[01:30] Maya Patel: Great question. GA for Dedicated first — that's reserved capacity on hosted infra, billing and contract side ready. Private is on a separate cadence, pilot expanding in March, we're hoping to move a couple of mid-market pilots into closed beta by the end of March. Private GA is still later H2, depends on a few security and packaging items.

[02:05] Noah Brooks: On infra — a couple wins. We shaved median tail latency by ~12% for chat workloads by improving KV cache eviction and changing batching heuristics. The continuous batching heuristics were slightly over-aggregating for low-latency customers, so we added a dynamic threshold. That cut cost for some customers but also kept SLOs tight. There's a short benchmark doc in the shared drive — link in chat. Also, early tests with the new kernel selection logic show better perf on A10X and A100 in some configs; still tuning.

[03:01] Ethan Li: Engineering update — we've closed 18 infra tickets in the last sprint, plus we shipped the rollout pipeline support for A/B model variants (canary + automatic fallback). This will reduce customer-facing incidents during deploys. We're also hiring more infra SREs — there are 6 reqs posted. Please refer candidates to People Ops.

[03:40] Sofia Chen: Research — model onboarding improvements: we added heuristics to pick quantization-friendly attention kernels and a light eval harness that runs perf + quality comparisons across model family variants. Early signals show QAT (quant-aware training) isn't necessary for many of our open model variants — just careful kernel selection helps. We did call out one regression with a 7B finetune where answer duplication occurs at longer contexts — working with the finetune team.

[04:25] Julian West: Sales / GTM — enterprise pipeline is healthy. A few larger expansion opportunities where Dedicated plus Private is in play. We saw a handful of RFPs where the buying centers are security + infra. Pricing experiments show customers are sensitive to per-token vs per-request billing for short prompt-heavy workloads; we'll surface some new packaging later this quarter.

[05:05] Liam O'Connor: Quick finance pulse — runway unchanged at the high level, revenue growth tracking vs plan, and we're being conservative on capex for next quarter. No surprises.

[05:30] Priya Shah: CS — onboarding NPS for pilot customers improved slightly after we shipped the onboarding checklist. We also added token level cost breakdowns to the console for customers in beta and that's gotten good feedback.

[06:00] Aria Nakamura: OK, couple of strategic notes. First, our thesis hasn't changed: serving is the moat. We need to stay disciplined on reliability and measurable economics. Second, competition is heating up — Anthropic and some cloud providers are pushing managed endpoints. We win on predictable economics and deployment flexibility, and we need to double down on case studies that show that. Third, leadership offsite planning — we'll schedule that in March, please fill the poll.

[07:12] Audience question (typed in chat): Can you remind us what the Dedicated SLA numbers will be?

[07:20] Maya Patel: The SLA targets are in the draft doc — 99.9% uptime target, p95 latency targets by model class (we'll share explicit numbers). We're intentionally conservative on the numbers until we've validated enough bookings.

[08:05] Speaker 2: Are we doing any changes to pricing for embeddings? I heard there might be a change.

[08:15] Julian West: We're exploring bundling and volume tiers for embeddings, yes. No final decisions yet. We'll pilot with a few existing customers. We want to avoid sudden changes for customers — it's more about new contracts and incentives.

[09:00] (Small technical interruption, audio glitch for ~10s)

[09:20] Noah Brooks: Two technical notes I want everyone to know — 1) autoscaler improvements cut eviction related restarts by ~30% in stage, 2) a small change to the rollout system will allow us to do regional routing per blue/green which helps capacity planning. The kernel-selection engine still has a few false positives on NVidia driver combos that make some 8-bit runs slower — we'll keep the fallback path for those runs.

[10:30] Sofia Chen: Research shoutout — congrats to the team that finished the eval harness, it makes it much easier to compare quality/latency trade-offs. Also, the eval sets for our critical apps have expanded, so regression alerts should be more meaningful.

[11:00] People Ops note (typed): Hiring bar update and interview calibration sessions next week.

[11:20] Aria Nakamura: On hiring — I want to emphasize we need to be thoughtful. We have strategic hires for infra, product, and enterprise sales. We also are focusing on leveling managers and mentorship.

[12:05] Q&A open floor:
[12:10] Employee: Any update on Private on-prem packaging? Customers ask about air-gapped installs and KMS/HSM integrations.

[12:25] Maya Patel: Yes — Private pilot includes a simplified on-prem bundle and initial KMS integration patterns. HSM is coming later, but we've scoped it. The air-gap packaging needs extra validation and a tighter install matrix; target is to have repeatable pilot installs by end of March.

[13:05] Employee: Any new enterprise security certifications (SOC2/ISO)?

[13:20] Priya Shah: We're progressing on SOC 2 Type II and started an ISO gap assessment. We expect SOC 2 Type II in the next quarter-ish. We're also adding audit log improvements to the console for customers who need longer retention.

[14:10] Employee: How are we measuring product-market fit for Dedicated vs Hosted?

[14:30] Maya Patel: Good question. We look at ARR coverage from bookings where Dedicated is explicit, renewal rates for customers who moved to Dedicated, and the lift in deal size for customers that add Private. Also, we track latency and cost-per-1M tokens as operational KPIs.

[15:20] Aria Nakamura: OK, a couple tactical asks: 1) leadership — prepare one slide each for the offsite about biggest risks and mitigation, 2) product — publish the roadmap deck and link in the company #product channel, 3) engineering — put a brief note in the infra channel about the kernel fallback behavior so customer-facing folks can communicate clearly.

[16:05] Quick lightning updates from teams (30–40s each):
[16:10] Growth: new referral program launched, small early signals on adoption.
[16:40] Solutions Eng: new benchmark scripts for customers, link in the chat.
[17:00] Customer Success: pilot onboarding templates published.

[18:00] Open AMA continued:
[18:05] Employee: Are we still prioritizing open models vs closed fine-tuned stacks?

[18:20] Sofia Chen: We still favor open models as the base for flexibility and cost, but we will support finetuned stacks when customers need specific behavior. It's a hybrid approach.

[19:10] Aria Nakamura: Thank you all. Final note — please fill out the post-all-hands survey, and leadership will follow up with the offsite poll.

Recap / Shared links: roadmap deck (link), Q1 metrics spreadsheet (link), Dedicated benchmark doc (link), hiring plan (link).

Transcript notes: auto-transcription had moderate noise on some technical terms (KV cache, quantization, A100/A10X), proper nouns sometimes mis-attributed in captions. Some chat references shown as "link in chat" for brevity.

End of meeting.
